nativeHelp.label: follow mode core
nativeHelp.claimText:
To join a party, first you must be invited by the leader (with the INVITE 
command).  Once you have been invited, you may type FOLLOW <username> to
start following that person.  While following you will move where they move
and will show up in their PARTY command.
To stop following, you may type LEAVE, your leader may type UNINVITE <you>,
or you may exit the game.

nativeHelp.label: follow BLIND/NORMAL
nativeHelp.claimText:
There are two types of following, BLIND and NORMAL.  If you are following 'BLIND', then you will not see any room descriptions as you move with
your party.  If you are following 'NORMAL', then you will see all the 
room descriptions normally as you move.
Syntax:
SET FOLLOW BLIND
SET FOLLOW NORMAL

nativeHelp.label: LEAVE
nativeHelp.claimText:
The leave command does a number of things depending on its use:
You can leave a party which you are following by typing LEAVE.
You can leave your broadcast group and switch to group 0 (no group)
by typing LEAVE when you are not in a party.
You can leave a gang by typing LEAVE GANG.

nativeHelp.label: SHARE
nativeHelp.claimText:
The SHARE command is used to share a certain amount of a currency
with either the members of your party or everyone in the room.  
The syntax of the command is:
SHARE <amount> <currency> [WITH <ROOM/PARTY>]
If you do not specify WITH ROOM or WITH PARTY, then PARTY is assumed.
If the amount you are sharing does not divide evenly among the people
in the room/party, then you will be left with the remainder.  In other
words, if you SHARE 5 GOLD and there are only 2 people other than yourself
in your party, each will receive 2 gold and you will be left with 1.
If you attempt to SHARE with anyone who is hidden or has their RECEIVE
set off, then they will not be included in the receipts of your sharing.

strongCorrelations.claim: Classic party capacity is six total characters including the leader.
NPC XP is awarded to active combatants rather than by party membership; monster currency is not automatically party-split; SHARE is the explicit manual currency distribution path.

Follower movement is resolved after the leader move and traverses the resulting door state. This supports the observed leader-opens/followers-pass case without inventing a party-wide key ownership transfer.
strongCorrelations.caveat: No separate native party-key-sharing primitive is claimed.

operatorHypotheses.claim: When a multi-member party leader leaves, the party disbands.
Quest commands are actor-local; party membership does not automatically grant quest command credit.
Death creates the dead character death pile and does not impose a native party wait timer.
Unexpected disconnect does not impose a native party wait timer; MegaMUD wait behavior is client-side.
